newsitem.title: CANADA: Poll shows strong support for Canada's Chretien.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows strong support for Canada's Chretien.

text.p: Most Canadians think Prime Minister Jean Chretien should lead national unity forces if there is another referendum on Quebec independence, according to a poll published on Monday in the Globe and Mail.

In the Environics poll, 56 percent of those surveyed across Canada said Chretien, recently re-elected, "is best able to deal with the (Quebec) situation and should remain to carry out his term as Prime Minister," the Toronto-based newspaper said.
Twenty-seven percent said Chretien should step down before the next referendum.
Outside Quebec, Chretien's native province, support for him was at 60 percent, while 23 percent said someone else should lead unity forces as Canada's prime minister.
Forty-five percent of Quebec respondents said Chretien should stay on as prime minister, while 37 percent said he should resign.

"The Globe and Mail/Environics poll numbers suggest that most Canadians are comfortable with the notion of Mr. Chretien playing a prominent role fighting the (Quebec) separatists during a third campaign on independence, despite his relative unpopularity in his home province and the fact that the federalists came within a whisker of losing the 1995 referendum," the newspaper said.

In October 1995, separatists lost a referendum on Quebec sovereignty by the wafer-thin margin of 49.4 percent to 50.6 percent. Chretien came under severe criticism from Canadian unity supporters who accused him of nearly losing the vote.

Quebec premier Lucien Bouchard has said he will hold another referendum on independence for the mainly French-speaking province if his separatist Parti Quebecois is re-elected in the next provincial election.
The provincial government's current mandate ends in September 1999, but the premier can call a vote at any time before then.
Chretien's Liberal Party won re-election to a second consecutive five-year term by a thin majority two months ago.
The Environics poll found that support for the federal Liberals had increased to 45 percent from the 39 percent popular vote they won in the election.
The poll surveyed 1,949 adult Canadians between July 7 and 30. The national margin of error was 2.2 percentage points, but regional figures had a higher potential margin of error.
